questions.stem:
Passage for Q1-Q5:
'Education is the most powerful (1)___ that you can use to change the world. A good education (2)___ a person with skills, knowledge, and the ability to think (3)___. However, access to quality education remains (4)___ in many parts of the world. Governments must invest in schools and teachers to ensure that every child has the (5)___ to learn.'

Q1: Choose the best word for blank (1).

options.option_text: weapon (correct: 'weapon you can use to change the world' — famous Mandela quote context; weapon here means tool/instrument ✓)
barrier (opposite meaning — barrier blocks change)
obstacle (same problem as barrier)
burden (burden = something heavy/oppressive — not positive)

questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Weapon' here is used metaphorically (as a powerful tool/instrument) — this paraphrases Nelson Mandela's famous quote: 'Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world.' In context, weapon = most effective tool.

questions.stem: Using the same education passage, Q2: Choose the best word for blank (2): 'A good education (2)___ a person with skills, knowledge...'

options.option_text: deprives (deprives = takes away — opposite)
equips (correct: 'equips a person with skills' = provides/arms with skills ✓)
burdens (carries a negative connotation; skills are positive)
confuses (wrong: confusion is not what education provides)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Equips a person with skills' means to provide or arm someone with the necessary tools/abilities. This is the standard collocation: 'equip with skills/knowledge'. Deprives (takes away), burdens (adds weight), confuses — all wrong.

questions.stem: Using the same education passage, Q3: Choose the best word for blank (3): '...the ability to think (3)___.'

options.option_text: irrationally (wrong: education aims for rational thinking)
critically (correct: 'ability to think critically' = to analyse and evaluate — key outcome of education ✓)
slowly (speed of thinking is irrelevant here)
selfishly (wrong: selfish thinking is not an educational goal)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Think critically' is a well-established educational term referring to the ability to analyse, evaluate, and form judgements. It collocates naturally with 'skills, knowledge, and the ability to think critically' — a standard trio in education discourse.

questions.stem: Using the same education passage, Q4: Choose the best word for blank (4): '...access to quality education remains (4)___ in many parts of the world.'

options.option_text: universal (wrong: the sentence follows 'however' — it contrasts the ideal with reality; universal = available to all, which contradicts the issue)
abundant (wrong: abundance contradicts the problem being described)
elusive (correct: 'remains elusive' = hard to achieve or find; fits the context of inequality in education access ✓)
guaranteed (wrong: guaranteed means assured — opposite of the problem)

questions.explanation: C is correct. The word follows 'However', signalling a contrast — the reality is that education access is NOT easy to achieve. 'Elusive' = difficult to find or achieve. The sentence says quality education 'remains elusive' in many parts of the world — meaning it's still hard to access.

questions.stem: Using the same education passage, Q5: Choose the best word for blank (5): '...ensure that every child has the (5)___ to learn.'

options.option_text: burden (wrong: burden is a negative term — children shouldn't have a 'burden to learn')
opportunity (correct: 'opportunity to learn' = a chance or right — standard collocation ✓)
obstacle (wrong: obstacle prevents learning)
responsibility (responsibility doesn't fit 'has the ___ to learn' in context; 'opportunity' fits better)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Has the opportunity to learn' is the standard phrase — it means having access to or a chance at learning. The passage talks about governments investing to ensure this — 'opportunity' (chance/right) fits perfectly. Burden/obstacle have negative meaning; responsibility changes the meaning.

questions.stem:
Passage for Q6-Q10:
'In recent years, technology has (6)___ the way people communicate. Social media platforms (7)___ millions to share information instantly across the globe. While this has many (8)___ effects, it has also led to the rapid (9)___ of misinformation. People must develop (10)___ literacy to navigate this digital landscape responsibly.'

Q6: Choose the best word for blank (6).

options.option_text: preserved (preserved = kept as is — opposite of what technology did to communication)
transformed (correct: technology has fundamentally changed/transformed communication ✓)
deteriorated (deteriorated = made worse — too negative and one-sided for the passage)
ignored (wrong: technology actively changed communication, not ignored it)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Transformed the way people communicate' = fundamentally changed it. The passage has a balanced tone (both positive and negative effects are mentioned), so 'deteriorated' is too negative and 'preserved' is opposite. 'Transformed' fits perfectly.

questions.stem: Using the technology passage, Q7: '...Social media platforms (7)___ millions to share information instantly...'

options.option_text: prevent (wrong: social media enables/allows sharing — opposite)
discourage (wrong: opposite of what social media does)
enable (correct: 'enable millions to share' = make it possible for millions ✓)
restrict (wrong: restriction is the opposite of what platforms do)

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Enable' = make possible. 'Social media platforms enable millions to share information' — this is the standard meaning. Enable collocates well: 'enable someone to do something'. Prevent/discourage/restrict are all antonyms in this context.

questions.stem: Using the technology passage, Q8: '...this has many (8)___ effects...'

options.option_text: destructive (wrong: the 'while...it has also led to' structure means (8) is the positive side)
beneficial (correct: the contrast 'While this has many beneficial effects, it has also led to misinformation' works perfectly ✓)
harmful (wrong: same issue as destructive — the 'while' clause needs a positive word)
negligible (negligible = very small/unimportant — contradicts 'many' in the sentence)

questions.explanation: B is correct. The sentence structure 'While this has many (8) effects, it has also led to...' sets up a contrast. The second clause mentions misinformation (negative), so the first clause needs a positive word. 'Beneficial' (= producing good results) creates the intended contrast.

questions.stem: Using the technology passage, Q9: '...it has also led to the rapid (9)___ of misinformation.'

options.option_text: decline (decline = decrease — but misinformation is spreading, not declining)
suppression (wrong: suppression = holding back — opposite of spread)
spread (correct: 'rapid spread of misinformation' = quick dissemination of false information ✓)
creation (creation = making — misinformation is spreading, not being created here)

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Rapid spread of misinformation' is a natural collocation. The passage describes social media enabling instant sharing — the downside is that false information can spread just as rapidly. 'Spread' captures this best. 'Dissemination' would also work but is not an option.

questions.stem: Using the technology passage, Q10: '...People must develop (10)___ literacy to navigate this digital landscape.'

options.option_text: physical (physical literacy relates to movement/sports — not digital)
financial (financial literacy = money management — not relevant here)
digital (correct: 'digital literacy' = the ability to use technology effectively and critically — directly relevant ✓)
scientific (scientific literacy relates to science — not this context)

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Digital literacy' is the established term for the skills needed to use digital technology effectively, including critically evaluating online information. The phrase 'navigate this digital landscape' is a strong contextual clue — the answer must be 'digital'. This is also a high-frequency exam term.
